title: a statement-position switch keeps TypeScript's fallthrough, break, and default behavior exactly
notes: The promise this pins — statement-position `switch` keeps ordinary TypeScript behavior, unlike the expression-position value `switch` — used to be carried by `statement-switch-keeps-typescript-fallthrough`. That case turned out to be rejected by real TypeScript with TS2678 for an unrelated reason (its scrutinee `"a"` has a literal type, so `case "b"` is not comparable to it), so it now pins the rejection and this case pins the fallthrough itself over a `string`-typed scrutinee TypeScript accepts. `classify("a")` must fall out of the matched clause into the next one and push both "a" and "b"; `classify("b")` must stop at its `break`; `classify("z")` must reach `default`. Any implementation that treats a statement `switch` like the expression form — one clause, no fallthrough — produces "a,b,d" and fails here.
